correctness.rationale: This assessment is for repairs/4/RESULT.md. The frozen proof at line 68 asserts invariance of the entire equal-width wedge, which is false: at alpha=1/2, mu=0, p=-2, z=p-delta and y=delta, one has r=1-(3/2)delta+O(delta^2) and z_next-p=-2delta+O(delta^2). The repair separately chooses the y-width after the z-width. The exact ratio update then contracts by at most (1+alpha)/2 plus a forcing smaller than the inward margin, and the negative quadratic term traps y. Taking reciprocals in the two ratio bounds gives affine bounds with slopes 1-O(1/N) and 1+O(1/N); on n<=NT these give u_n comparable to n+1. Independently checking the slow jet gives q=-alpha(1+alpha)/[2(1-alpha)^3] and b=(1-6alpha^2-alpha^3)/[6(1-alpha)^3]. The slaving error is bounded by convolution with a geometric ratio even after comparison with y_n^3. The repaired reciprocal recurrence discards only terms whose absolute sum is bounded; its weighted harmonic part has coefficient (a^2-b)/a=B and weight exp(-c lambda t) uniformly away from t=0, for both detuning signs and at lambda=0. The host scaling follows from the linear term of the slaving graph. The theorem and coefficients are unchanged. The checker was inspected, not executed; it does not establish trapping or uniformity.

value.rationale: The threshold is set by the model's bifurcation and the 1/N window by the linear-time crossover. The new term quantifies how the common leading clock is corrected at finite horizon; it gives a positive explicit coefficient independent of fixed positive initial data, and shows how detuning acts on the logarithm while fast-transient effects enter only at bounded order. The repair justifies the regime needed for those conclusions rather than changing the scientific target.
